chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you arrive at Mina, say: O Allah, this is Mina, and it is from what You have favored upon us among the rituals. So I ask You to favor upon us with what You have favored upon Your prophets. Indeed, I am Your servant and in Your hold.'

Then you should pray Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, the last Isha, and Fajr there; and the Imam prays Dhuhr there, and nothing else is permissible for him. It is permissible for you to pray elsewhere if you are unable. Then you join them at Arafat.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the boundary of Mina is from Al-Aqaba to the valley of Muhassar.'

key_terms.الْعَقَبَة: Al-Aqaba, a landmark defining the boundary of Mina
key_terms.عَرَفَات: Arafat, the main station of Hajj
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a sacred site near Mecca used for Hajj rituals
key_terms.وَادِي مُحَسِّر: Valley of Muhassar, another landmark defining the boundary of Mina

ai.seo_question: What are the specific prayers and supplications required when arriving at Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the ritual etiquette for arriving at Mina, emphasizing a supplication that links the pilgrim's status to the blessings granted to the Prophets, thereby reinforcing the Shia emphasis on imitative devotion. It clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the Imam's obligatory single prayer (Dhuhr) and the pilgrim's flexibility, while precisely defining Mina's boundaries from the Aqaba to Wadi Muhassir, a key reference for Shia fiqh of Hajj.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you end up to Mina, so say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! This is Mina, and it is from what You<sup>azwj</sup> have Favoured wih upon us, from the rituals. So I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> to Favour upon us with what You<sup>azwj</sup> have Favoured upon Your<sup>azwj</sup> Prophets<sup>as</sup>. So, rather, I am Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant, and in Your<sup>azwj</sup> Hold’.

Then you should Pray Al-Zohar, and Al-Asr, and Al-Magrib, and Al-Isha the last, and Al-Fajr, at it; and the Prayer-leader would Pray Al-Zohr at it, not having any leeway (for anything else) except for that, and there is leeway upon you that you Pray elsewhere if you are not able (upon Praying at Mina). Then you can join up with them (the people) at Arafaat’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And a boundary of Mina is from Aqaba up to the Muhassar valley’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and af-Fadf ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya and ibn abu ‘Umayr Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When you arrive in Mina’ say this, ‘O Lord, this is Mina’ which You have granted to us so we perform our acts (of devotion to You). I appeal before You to grant us what You granted to Your prophets. I am only Your servant in Your control.’

Thereafter perform your al-Zuhr, al-‘Asr, al-Maghrib, al-‘Isha’ al-’Akhirah and the morning Salawat (prayers). The Imam must perform al-Zuhr Salat (prayer) and he has no choice but you have the choice to perform anywhere you choose if you cannot perform. Thereafter join them in ‘Arafat.’
He (the Imam) said that the boundaries of Mina’ are al-‘Aqabah and al-Muhassar valley.’”
